fields.features_heading: What a Restaurant Page Needs to Work
fields.features_subheading: Each part below decides whether a request reaches the person who can say yes, and Emergent changes any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
The menu for this offer only

Show the dishes and prices that belong to the offer, such as the five courses of a tasting dinner. Link to the full menu once, at the bottom, for the guest who asks for it.
fields.feature_2:
A number a thumb can reach

Put the phone number in a tap-to-call button near the top, with the street address and a directions link under it. Give the guest who prefers to call a way to do it without typing.
fields.feature_3:
A row for every request

Each request lands in a database you own with the guest's name and party size, plus the date asked for. A status column lets the manager mark each row Confirmed or Declined.
fields.feature_4:
An alert to whoever confirms

Send each request by email or to a Slack channel the front of house reads. The alert puts the party size and a callback number in front of the manager working that night's shift.
fields.feature_5:
The notice the kitchen needs

Print how far ahead a request has to arrive, such as 48 hours for a catering order. Put that cutoff right next to the date field, where a guest reads it before picking a date.
fields.feature_6:
A web address guests know

Publish the page on the domain already printed on your menus and receipts, or on a subdomain of it for events and catering. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

fields.tab_content_1:
Rosalind books any table of 8 or more

Peppervine Bistro asks for the party size before it shows a time. A request for 8 or more guests skips the time picker and emails Rosalind Haddix, the events manager, who calls back to plan the room. Smaller parties pick a table time on the spot. Of 64 requests this week, 9 went to Rosalind and 55 picked a time.
fields.tab_content_2:
Orders that reach 50 guests go to Teo

Stonewick Smokehouse prices catering by headcount. Its quote form asks for the date, the number of guests, and pickup or delivery. Every order for 50 or more guests goes to Teo Beaty, the catering lead, and smaller orders go to the kitchen's list. This month Teo got 12 of 31 requests, and 19 went to the kitchen.
fields.tab_content_3:
After 40 seats, every name joins the waitlist

Lark Hollow Tavern has 40 seats for its $95 New Year's Eve tasting menu, with each course listed beside the form. Once the 40th seat is reserved, the form takes waitlist names, and the manager offers any canceled seat to the first name. So far 14 people have joined the waitlist.
fields.tab_content_4:
Westvale gets its own list of 138 signups

Sartino's Pizzeria is opening a second location in Westvale. Its signup page asks for an email address and one question: which location would you visit, Westvale or Downtown? Of 212 signups so far, the 138 who picked Westvale get the opening-night invite, and the 74 who picked Downtown stay on the regular list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Restaurant Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a restaurant landing page that sends each party, catering or event request to the person who confirms it.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the offer in plain numbers
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Show the dishes you will serve
fields.howto_step_1_des: Make one page for each offer, such as large parties or catering, and point each ad or flyer at its own page. A guest who came for the holiday dinner should not have to hunt for it on the full menu.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the form with the number of guests. It decides what the page offers next and who hears about the request. Put it ahead of the calendar and the contact details.
fields.howto_step_3_des: State the date, the price per guest, and what the price covers, such as 4 courses and coffee. Put all of it above the form, where the full cost is on screen before the first field.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use 3 or 4 photos of dishes from this offer, shot in your own dining room. Keep them short enough that the form still sits near the top of the page on a phone.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide who hears about each request
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name one person for each kind of request, such as the events manager for large parties and the catering lead for big orders. Send each request to that person, and to no one else.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the message the guest sees after sending: when someone will reply, and the number to call if the date is close. Promise a reply time you can meet every day of the week.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and send a test request
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the offer and who hears about each request, and Emergent builds the page from that prompt. Send a test request from your phone, then check the new row in your database and the alert.

faq_plan.q: What is a restaurant landing page?
faq_plan.a: A restaurant landing page is a single web page built around one offer, such as a large-party booking or a holiday dinner, with one form for that offer. It leaves out the full site's menu bar, and its only next steps are the form and the phone number.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a restaurant landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide the offer and who confirms each request, then describe both to Emergent's AI landing page builder in a sentence or two. Emergent builds the page and the database behind it, and any later change is another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should the form on a restaurant landing page ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the guest's name, a phone number, the date and time, and the number of guests. Add one optional notes line for things like a birthday or a high chair, and leave everything else for the confirmation call. On a page Emergent builds, each answer is saved as a column in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a restaurant landing page take private event bookings?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the date and the guest count, then send each request to whoever runs the private room, since that person knows which dates are still open. A wedding landing page works from the other side: it collects RSVPs from the couple's guests for one date, while your page books the room for the dinner.

faq_plan.q: How do I get people to a restaurant landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give every place you promote it its own link, such as a QR code on the table tent and the link in your social profile. Tag each link, and you can see which one sent the requests that came in. The app Emergent builds can save that tag on every request row.

faq_plan.q: Should a restaurant landing page cover one location or all of them?
faq_plan.a: Cover one location when the locations differ in hours or in the offer itself. One page per location keeps each request with the right manager and lets each page show its own address. If the offer is the same everywhere, use one page and ask which location the guest wants.

faq_plan.q: How do I promote a new menu with a restaurant landing page?
faq_plan.a: Build a page for the new menu alone, with the first date it is served and three or four of its dishes, and ask visitors to sign up for a first-week table. It follows the same pattern as a product launch landing page: one release, announced with a list of the people who want it first.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect email signups on a restaurant landing page?
faq_plan.a: Offer something specific in return, such as first word on the seasonal menu or an invite to a tasting night. Ask for the email address and nothing else, or add a birthday month if you plan to send a birthday offer. Emergent is free to start: the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What headline should a restaurant landing page use?
faq_plan.a: Use the offer and its date as the headline, in the words a guest would say, such as Sunday brunch for 10 or more, booked by Thursday. Put the price or the guest count in the line under it, and keep the restaurant's name for the logo.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a restaurant landing page for a pop-up dinner?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Build the page around the pop-up's dates and address, take reservations or signups for those nights, and take the page down once the last night is over. It works like a real estate landing page made for one open house: one address and a single form.

plan.angle: A restaurant site already carries the menu, the hours and the address; a restaurant landing page does one job that the site does badly, such as a large-party request, a catering quote, a ticketed holiday dinner or a list for a new location. This page shows four of those pages with the form, the rule behind it and the row each request leaves in a database the owner keeps, then gives seven build steps an owner or general manager can follow. It makes no health-code, liquor, payment or delivery-platform claims, and the wedding sibling stays out of the headings.
